The `DLAGENTS` override is defined at the top level, which could in theory allow arbitrary command execution during source downloads — however, `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does not trigger downloads or use `DLAGENTS`, so this poses no risk during this specific command.

There is no command substitution (e.g., `$(...)` or `` `...` ``) in global variable definitions, and no immediate execution of external commands or scripts. The URL and source array use standard templating with `pkgver`, which is safe. While the comment notes a workaround for a CDN anti-bot measure, it does not introduce active malicious code. All content is consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for binary packages.

Thus, sourcing this PKGBUILD for `--printsrcinfo` is safe.
</details>

No unexpected network requests, code execution, or file modifications occur. Systemd service installation is standard and follows Arch best practices (not auto-enabling).
